correctness.rationale: Every symmetric subset with center c is contained in C_c=K∩(2c-K). Convex Minkowski interpolation C_tc+(1-t)d supersets tC_c+(1-t)C_d; planar Brunn–Minkowski gives concavity of sqrt(area C_c). The odd dihedral rotation orbit averages to origin, giving optimal C_0. The reflected n centers interlace into 2n uniformly spaced circle centers. The limiting disk for any radial ray is the one with smallest dot product, so its quadratic yields s(delta)=-r cos delta+sqrt(1-r² sin² delta), delta in [-pi/k,pi/k]. Exact integration of k sectors gives F(k,r). Each generating vertex violates its reflected disk as 2r_n>1, giving strict proper inclusion. An independent mpmath evaluation confirms beta(3)=0.8403426028066864, beta(5)=0.9479862949042737; independent symbolic Taylor of F verifies the coefficients through n^-4. All-n proof is analytic, not ray-grid quadrature.
residual_risks: A symmetry maximizing center is established, not uniqueness; no monotonicity across odd n claimed.

value.rationale: The Kovner–Besicovitch maximum centrally symmetric inner-area fraction is a classical natural asymmetry invariant. Computing its exact value simultaneously for every regular odd Reuleaux polygon, with a global symmetry-center theorem and sharp second-order and fourth-order convergence to symmetry, is a substantive natural family result beyond one benchmark. Potential use in comparisons of convex constant-width asymmetry measures.
residual_risks: No proof of monotonicity or of an irregular-polygon extremal classification, and no assertion of absolute historical priority.

final_claim: For regular width-one Reuleaux odd-n-gons n>=3 defined by n equally spaced disks with center-circle radius r_n=(2cos(pi/(2n)))^-1, the maximal centrally symmetric inner-area fraction is F(2n,r_n)/F(n,r_n), attained by K_n∩(-K_n), with F the displayed exact polar disk-intersection area and expansion 1-pi^2/(8n^2)-25pi^4/(1536n^4)+O(n^-6).
limitations: All odd n>=3 regular disk intersections of common width; no uniqueness of symmetric maximizing center, no irregular Reuleaux classification.
